nodes.description: Address of the game owner; used as the only access-control guard for lock, unlock, releaseFunds and initial own().
Boolean flag that gates the payout branch inside bet(); can be toggled by the owner.
Payable betting function; checks random parity, msg.value == 1 ether and !locked, then transfers 2 ether to msg.sender.
Sets locked = true, but only if gameOwner == msg.sender.
Sets locked = false, but only if gameOwner == msg.sender.
Sets gameOwner to an arbitrary address when gameOwner is zero or when called by the current owner (ownership takeover/wash logic).
Owner-only function that sends amount * 1 ether to msg.sender via a low-level call.
View pseudo-random generator derived from block.timestamp and block.difficulty (predictable/miner-influenced).
Payable fallback function that forwards all value into bet().
Caller-controlled address used as access-control subject and as the recipient of all ether transfers.
Miner-controllable timestamp used as entropy for random().
msg.sender.call.value(2 ether)() low-level value transfer inside bet() with no gas limit and no state guard on re-entry.
msg.sender.call.value(amount * (1 ether))() low-level value transfer inside releaseFunds().
Unchecked multiplication amount * (1 ether) in releaseFunds(), susceptible to silent overflow under solc 0.4.24.
Parameter 'owner' of own(); the new owner address chosen by the caller.
Parameter 'amount' of releaseFunds(); caller-supplied multiplier for the ether transfer.

edges.reason: bet() executes the low-level value call to msg.sender before any state change or guard update.
msg.sender is the destination of the 2 ether transfer, so an attacker-controlled contract receives control mid-execution.
The external call hands control to the caller, which can re-enter bet()/fallback() while locked is still false.
bet() reads the locked flag to decide whether the payout branch runs.
lock() gates on gameOwner, an address-only ownership check.
lock() compares msg.sender against gameOwner to authorise the state change.
lock() writes the locked state variable.
unlock() gates on gameOwner.
unlock() compares msg.sender against gameOwner to authorise the state change.
unlock() writes the locked state variable.
own() assigns gameOwner, transferring privileged control of the contract.
The owner parameter is stored directly into the gameOwner state variable.
own() permits takeover whenever gameOwner == msg.sender or is still address(0).
releaseFunds() gates the ether transfer on gameOwner.
releaseFunds() authorises the transfer only when gameOwner == msg.sender.
releaseFunds() performs the unchecked low-level value call to msg.sender.
msg.sender receives the funds and thus regains control during the transfer.
The amount parameter drives the size of the payout in releaseFunds().
The amount parameter is multiplied by 1 ether without overflow protection.
The unchecked product determines the value sent by the low-level call.
random() derives its result from block.timestamp, making the outcome miner-influenced.
The value returned by random() feeds the modulo parity check inside bet().
The payable fallback forwards all received value straight into bet(), providing an automatic re-entry path.

normalization_plan.reason: Parameter 'owner' has no independent security meaning; it exists only to be written into gameOwner by own(), so it collapses into the own() function node.
Parameter 'amount' is used only to size the payout inside releaseFunds(); it folds into the releaseFunds() function node that performs the transfer.
